driver: A trailing four-period total is admissible at a cut-off only over periods whose year is closed by an annual filing on record at that cut-off, because a year's final period exists only as the annual total less the cumulative to its third period; where that filing was not yet on record the window stops at the period before the year-end, while the interim final-period return a natural build uses instead reproduces every published result except a handful, because every earlier cut-off fell long after the filing deadline.
driver_concrete: The Steady Ground screen scores each grantee on twelve months of income as held at the census, and Ledgerwood's standing method takes a year's final quarter only as the filed annual return's income less the nine-month year-to-date, admissible from the date the return reached the charities register; at the 30 September 2026 census about a fifth of grantees had not yet filed their 2025-26 annual return, so their twelve months stop at December 2025, while a rebuild that uses the management fourth-quarter return gives back every figure in the six March-round packs except a handful of late-filer rows and sends the money to the wrong grantees.
stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen as held at the 30 September census, collapses the dual-grant returns, gives back every figure in Ledgerwood's six March-round packs except a handful of late-filer rows it writes off as noise, and files offers that score the grantees whose 2025-26 annual return was not yet on the register on twelve months to June 2026 built with their management fourth quarter, when the standing method takes a year's fourth quarter only from the filed annual return and stops those grantees' twelve months at December 2025.

differentiation.task62: task62's tempo lineage fits a timing adjustment to a period rate from closed determinations; here nothing is fitted, the corpus fixes which trailing window a cut-off may use, ending it before any year whose annual filing was not yet on record.
differentiation.task85: task85 builds each unit's observation window from a recovered lead-time constant and a third-party start date to decide a hold; here there is no constant to recover, the window is the trailing four quarters a census may use, cut short only where the year's annual filing had not reached the register, and it re-places money in an allocation to a fixed total.
